text:
matt: Heads-up — saw a sharp drop in prefix cache hit for model=redwood-open-v2 on route=/summarize for tenant=acme-inc. Token-saved rate down ~42% over last 3h, traffic roughly constant. Grafana panel: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123

sasha: oof. do we have per-model / per-route / per-customer slices for the hit-rate? want to see if this is isolated to acme or wider. any recent kernel/batching changes deployed?

perf-bot: ALERT: CACHE_HIT_DROP for /summarize (tenant: acme-inc, model: redwood-open-v2) — threshold 25% exceeded — triggered at 2023-11-01T12:04:12Z.

jenna: i pulled the panel and made a quick query. looks like the hit-rate delta correlates with kernel version rollout on the gpupool-42 nodes. query i used:

```
# promql
sum by (tenant, model, route, kernel_version) (
  increase(prefix_cache_hits_total[1h])
) / sum by (tenant, model, route, kernel_version) (
  increase(prefix_cache_requests_total[1h])
)
```

link to panel with kernel_version split: https://grafana.internal/d/xyz789

kai: i started a profile dump on an affected node. early signal: pack-batch-v2 scheduler increased the number of partial batches which increases KV cache churn (more unique KV keys observed per sequence) -> evictions +18% in the last deploy window. also saw longer scheduling latency for small sequences which changes batching distribution.

matt: that matches a spike in kv_cache_evictions_total I can see in tenant-slice. warmup prefetch rate also dropped because keys didn't match our normalized prefixes. here's the snippet from the warmup logs where we see the mismatch:

```
WARN warmup: key mismatch for promptkey="User: What is the summary of...\n(very long prompt, 3000 chars)" -> normalized_key="User: What is the summary ..." (truncated)
```

sasha: sounds like two orthogonal issues: kernel+batching changed the runtime behavior, and key derivation changed effective cardinality for the cache. options: rollback kernel rollout on gpupool-42, or change key normalization & warmup to be robust to entropy. which is faster?

jenna: for short term i recommend a two-prong approach: 1) add a dashboard filter and alert dimension on kernel_version so ops can quickly identify regressions; 2) add token-saved per-tenant panel and a small SLI alert (e.g., token-saved drop >20% for 30m). Action items below:
- add kernel_version to the hit-rate panels (i'll PR the grafana json)
- create per-tenant token-saved timeseries (sum tokens_saved by tenant, model, route)
- add SLO alert: token-saved-drop >20% for 30m -> page on-call

kai: i'll run a regression bisect on the pack-batch-v2 change and try toggling the kernel flag in the pool. also working on a key-normalization patch to reduce entropy: lowercasing, canonical whitespace, and truncating to 1024 chars before hashing. will test warmup job with normalized keys in staging.

matt: can we also capture a sample of offending prompt keys and the corresponding KV key lengths so we can quantify the entropy increase? put them in a temp S3 bucket with redaction.

kai: yep — grabbing samples now and pushing to s3://redwood-dev/warmup-samples/1698765432. I'll redact PII and include counts per key-length bin.

matt: OK assign owners: jenna -> grafana + alerts, kai -> bisect + key-normalization PR, sasha -> coordinate rollback decision if bisect points to kernel. i'll follow up with customer success to flag acme-inc and see if they report user impact. :thumbsup:

jenna: PR opened for kernel_version split on panels and token-saved charts. small note: keep the kernel_version label cardinality low (only pool-level tags) so panels stay performant.

perf-bot: NOTE: incident ticket created: INC-2023-4579 (prefix-cache hit regression) — assignees: jenna, kai, sasha, matt.

matt: thanks all — let's aim for a decision in the next 2 hours. if bisect is slow, fallback is to pin gpupool-42 to pack-batch-v1 and re-run warmup.

sasha: copy. i'll prep the rollback runbook and post it here if we need to execute.

kai: starting bisect now. will report findings in this thread.
